results.content: # Measurement Errors. ## Measurement Errors: Definition, Types, Examples, Causes, and Prevention. These discrepancies are known as measurement errors, and understanding them is essential to improving accuracy, precision, and the reliability of results. ## **What Is a Measurement Error?**. A measurement error is the difference between a measured value and the true value of the quantity being measured. These errors can arise from instrument limitations, human mistakes, environmental factors, or procedural flaws. For instance, a technician entering a wrong reading or using an improperly calibrated micrometer can lead to a measurable error. ## Types of Errors in Measurement. **Measurement errors are generally categorized into three primary types:**. * **Systematic Errors**: These are predictable and repeatable errors due to flaws in the measuring system or methodology:. * **Random Errors**: These occur unpredictably and vary with each measurement, often caused by:. ## **Practical Examples of Measurement Errors**. * A scale error in measurement may happen if the measuring scale itself is miscalibrated. * Human error in measurement includes parallax errors, misreading instruments, or data entry mistakes. * A gross error example is reading a value while the instrument is off-zero. ## **What Causes Measurement Errors?**. **The sources of error in measurement include**. * **Personal errors** – mistakes by the person performing the measurement. ## **How to Reduce Errors in Measurement**. ## **Measurement Errors in Metrology, Research, and Industry**. In professional settings, measurement error is not just an inaccuracy- it’s a quantifiable uncertainty that can impact safety, quality, and compliance. * In regulated industries like aerospace or pharmaceuticals, minimizing measurement error is critical for product validation and audit readiness. When combining multiple measurements, their errors propagate:. **Example**: If a length measurement is 10.0 ± 0.2 cm and width is 5.0 ± 0.1 cm, then area = 50.0 cm² with a propagated error of ±2.5%. ## Closing Thoughts on Measurement Errors. Understanding and minimizing measurement errors- whether gross, systematic, or random – is fundamental for ensuring reliable data. By identifying errors early and applying the right corrective strategies, professionals across research, manufacturing, and quality control can enhance confidence in their measurements and maintain process excellence.

results.content: # Point-of-Care High-Sensitivity Assay for Troponin I Compares Well With Central Labs. A point-of-care (POC) high-sensitivity assay for cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) shows diagnostic accuracy comparable to what’s achieved by central laboratory assays and could potentially be a useful addition to early-triage algorithms for patients who present to emergency departments (EDs) with chest pain, according to an analysis from the APACE study. “When comparing our data to previously published data on other POC hs-cTnI assays, we found that the efficacy of the POC hs-cTnI SpinChip 0/1-hour algorithm—measured by the number of patients who could be triaged for rule-in and rule-out—was higher than that of other POC hs-cTnI assays,” Koechlin said in an email. He added that the findings need to be confirmed by further studies comparing the SpinChip algorithm with the other POC hs-cTnI assays that have demonstrated similar abilities and can be embedded in early-triage algorithms. In a prior APACE analysis, researchers found that the TriageTrue POC hs-cTnI assay (Quidel) had high diagnostic accuracy for NSTEMI compared to assays requiring a central lab. Koechlin said a direct comparison of all POC hs-cTnI assays within the same patient cohort is necessary to evaluate potential differences among them. “Moreover, further research should investigate whether the use of POC hs-cTn assays in emergency departments, given their shorter turnaround time compared to central laboratory hs-cTn assays, leads to quicker triage and, subsequently, improvements in both medical and economic outcomes,” he added. and so is how you handle having two assays functioning in a hospital—one for point-of-care and one for the central laboratory,” Jaffe said, adding that while he sees the POC assays as a good thing, an argument could be made that having two systems could increase the risk for physician interpretation error. For the study, published this week in the *Journal of the American College of Cardiology*, Koechlin and colleagues compared the POC SpinChip assay with two central laboratory assays for troponin: Architect (Abbott) and Elecsys (Roche). “The introduction of POC hs-cTn assays will broaden the range of medical settings where patients can benefit from hs-cTn testing,” Koechlin told TCTMD. ## Point-of-Care High-Sensitivity Assay for Troponin I Compares Well With Central Labs.

results.title: Ten types of dimensional and geometrical measurement error
results.content: These types of measurement error are due to measurement procedures and the structural elements of an instrument #### Wahyudin Syam In any dimensional and geometrical measurements, different types of measurement error decrease the accuracy of the measurements. These types of measurement error can be classified into two general categories: * Measurement error related to measurement procedures * Measurement error related to structural elements of measuring instruments Examples of error related to measurement procedures are Abbe error, Sine and cosine error, datum error, zeroing error, misalignment error, error due to surface roughness and non-technical error. Abbe error is caused due to the measurement axis and motion axis of a measuring instrument do not coincident each other. These two non-coincident axes cause any small angular errors of the measuring arm of the instrument will be amplified and translated into Abbe error (figure 1). Figure 1 shows the illustration of Abbe offset, Abbe error, measurement axis, motion axis and angular error of an instrument. In figure 2, the optical axis (the motion axis) has an offset (not coincident) with the encoder axis (measurement axis) and cause Abbe error in measurement reading. In figure 3, cosine error is due to the motion of an instrument (or of a measured part) is not perpendicular with the feature of a part measured by the instrument. Although in micrometre scale, for measurement with accuracy at micrometre or higher level, these small errors are very significant and cause an instrument cannot be used for the measurement of parts with very tight tolerances. Error due to deviations from kinematic design principle All measuring instruments, they are assembled from many components. Geometrical deviation on components will cause measurement errors on an instrument. Any deviations from this standard temperature when performing measurements will cause errors due to part and instrument material expansions. Geometrical expansion and shrinkage of parts and instruments’ components will directly translated to measurement errors. Error related to structural loop In any measuring instruments, there are three force loops act on the instruments. Non-technical error is caused by the mistakes of operators who perform measurements with specific instruments. Reading error is an error due to an operator incorrectly read measurement results from an instrument.
